# clinical baselines seen in the reference data. Widened the QRS complex components 
# (Q, R, S widths) slightly to remove the unnatural "spiky" appearance and better 
# approximate a physiological 80-100ms QRS duration. Increased pink noise slightly 
# to maintain realistic low-frequency baseline wander without high-frequency fuzz.
# =============================================================================

FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_pink_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f pink noise for realistic physiological baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / (f ** 0.5)
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets

    return pink / np.std(pink)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)

    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)

    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(10, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 30) * np.pi / 180.0
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(15, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.22)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 2.2)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)

    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)

        p_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.18, -0.14)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)
        
        q_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.022, -0.016)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.022, 0.032)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)

            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width

            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.04)

            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)

            sigma_down = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
            dt_t = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_down
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.3, 0.5) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)

            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological 1/f Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander

    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

    pink_I = generate_pink_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.10)
    pink_II = generate_pink_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.10)

import os

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: Addressed morphological discrepancies by widening the QRS complex 
# components (R-wave in particular) to better match physiological durations 
# (80-100ms) and significantly reducing high-frequency and pink noise levels. 
# The previous noise levels were obscuring the repolarization features (T-waves) 
# and creating an uncharacteristically fuzzy baseline compared to real clinical 
# recordings.
# =============================================================================

FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_pink_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f pink noise for realistic physiological baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / (f ** 0.5)
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    pink = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return pink / np.std(pink)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)

    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(45.0, 95.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)

    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(10, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 30) * np.pi / 180.0
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(15, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.22)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 2.2)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)

    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.012, 0.018)

    twa_delta = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) if has_twa else 0.0

    # 2. Beat Generation (with Heart Rate Variability)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.035)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.035)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.04, 0.08)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.04)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.25) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.20) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)
            
        else:
            # LQT3: Late-onset T wave (long isoelectric ST segment)

            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological 1/f Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander
    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

# (Q, R, S widths) to better match physiological durations (80-100ms), preventing 
# the previous "spiky" artifact appearance. Additionally, significantly reduced 
# the amplitudes of high-frequency white noise, pink noise, and respiratory wander 
# to match the cleaner baseline fidelity observed in real clinical recordings.

DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"

    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_pink_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f pink noise for realistic physiological baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / (f ** 0.5)
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets

    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

    """

    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)

    """Generates 1/f pink noise for realistic physiological baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: Reduced artificial high-frequency noise to better match the 
# smooth baseline of real clinical recordings. Adjusted QRS proportions 
# (slightly wider and lower max amplitude) to prevent unrealistic QRS-to-T 
# wave ratios. Enhanced the distinctness of the LQT2 bifid T-wave and 
# expanded the variance of electrical axes to increase physiological diversity 
# and address inter-sample similarity discrepancies.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_pink_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f pink noise for realistic physiological baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / (f ** 0.5)
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    pink = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return pink / np.std(pink)

def generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx, seed):
    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Subject-Specific Physiological Parameters
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm (LQT1 often has mild bradycardia)
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(45.0, 95.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(10, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-30, 45) * np.pi / 180.0 # Expanded variance
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(0, 90) * np.pi / 180.0            # Expanded variance
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.25)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8) # Reduced max to prevent extreme QRS/T ratios
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    # Wave widths (adjusted for physiological 80-100ms QRS)
    p_width = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
    q_width = np.random.uniform(0.008, 0.012)
    r_width = np.random.uniform(0.010, 0.015) # Slightly wider for realism
    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.012, 0.018)
    
    # T-wave Alternans (TWA) for severe cases
    has_twa = (qtc > 0.52) and (np.random.rand() > 0.5)
    twa_delta = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) if has_twa else 0.0
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Beat Generation (with Heart Rate Variability)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    num_beats = int(DURATION / (rr_mean * 0.7)) + 5
    
    resp_rate = np.random.uniform(0.2, 0.35) # Hz
    rr_intervals = rr_mean + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * np.arange(num_beats)) 
    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)
    beat_times -= (beat_times[0] - np.random.uniform(0.1, rr_mean))
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. ECG Waveform Synthesis
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i, beat_t in enumerate(beat_times):
        if beat_t > DURATION + 1.0:
            break
        if beat_t < -1.0:
            continue
            
        rr = rr_intervals[i]
        # Bazett's formula: QT = QTc * sqrt(RR)
        qt = qtc * np.sqrt(rr)
        
        # --- P, Q, R, S Waves ---
        p_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.18, -0.14)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)
        
        q_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.020, -0.015)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.030)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start
            
            # Symmetrical shaping spanning exactly from S-end to QT-end
            sigma = t_duration / 5.0
            dt_t = st_start + 2.5 * sigma
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.7) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            # Sharper peaks and wider notch distance to ensure distinct bifid morphology
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.030)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.06, 0.10)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.030)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.25) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.20) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            amp2_I = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)
            
        else:
            # LQT3: Late-onset T wave (long isoelectric ST segment)
            sigma_up = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.03)
            sigma_down = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
            dt_t = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_down
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.3, 0.5) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological 1/f Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander
    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))
    
    # 1/f Pink noise for realistic low-frequency drift
    pink_I = generate_pink_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.03, 0.08)
    pink_II = generate_pink_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.03, 0.08)
    
    # Powerline interference
    pl_freq = np.random.choice([50.0, 60.0])
    pl_amp = np.random.uniform(0.005, 0.015)
    pl_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    powerline_I = pl_amp * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    powerline_II = pl_amp * 1.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    
    # High-frequency muscle (EMG) noise - reduced for cleaner, more realistic baseline
    noise_level = np.random.uniform(0.001, 0.004)
    hf_noise_I = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    hf_noise_II = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    
    lead_I += resp_wander_I + pink_I + powerline_I + hf_noise_I
    lead_II += resp_wander_II + pink_II + powerline_II + hf_noise_II

    ecg_signal = np.stack([lead_I, lead_II], axis=1)
    
    return ecg_signal

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
    
    for i in range(N_SAMPLES):
        sample_seed = RANDOM_SEED + i
        ecg_sample = generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx=i, seed=sample_seed)
        
        filename = f"lngqt_sample_{i:03d}.npy"
        filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)
        np.save(filepath, ecg_sample)
        
    print(f"Successfully generated {N_SAMPLES} LQTS ECG samples in '{OUTPUT_DIR}'.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: 
# 1. Constrained electrical axes (P, R, T) to physiological normal ranges 
#    (45-75 degrees) to ensure concordant, clearly visible, and positive 
#    T-waves in Leads I and II, preventing unrealistic inversions or flatlining.
# 2. Redesigned T-wave morphology generation to strictly follow the blueprint:
#    - LQT1: Now uses a symmetrical Gaussian spanning the exact ST segment.
#    - LQT2 & LQT3: Adjusted widths (sigmas) to be physiologically realistic 
#      (wider than previous tiny spikes) while maintaining their specific shapes.
# 3. Sharpened QRS complex widths and reduced baseline wander amplitudes to 
#    better match the clean, distinct morphology seen in real clinical samples.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

def generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx, seed):
    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Subject-Specific Physiological Parameters
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(50.0, 90.0)  # bpm (LQT often has mild bradycardia)
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Constrain axes to normal physiological range to ensure positive, concordant waves in I and II
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(45, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(150, 180) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(150, 180) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 15) * np.pi / 180.0 # Concordant with QRS
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(45, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.20)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.30)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    # Wave widths (sharpened for realistic QRS morphology)
    p_width = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.020)
    q_width = np.random.uniform(0.006, 0.010)
    r_width = np.random.uniform(0.008, 0.012)
    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.008, 0.012)
    
    # T-wave Alternans (TWA) for severe cases
    has_twa = (qtc > 0.52) and (np.random.rand() > 0.5)
    twa_delta = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) if has_twa else 0.0
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Beat Generation (with Heart Rate Variability)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    num_beats = int(DURATION / (rr_mean * 0.7)) + 5
    
    resp_rate = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.35) # Hz
    rr_intervals = rr_mean + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * np.arange(num_beats)) 
    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)
    beat_times -= (beat_times[0] - np.random.uniform(0.1, rr_mean))
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. ECG Waveform Synthesis
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i, beat_t in enumerate(beat_times):
        if beat_t > DURATION + 1.0:
            break
        if beat_t < -1.0:
            continue
            
        rr = rr_intervals[i]
        # Bazett's formula: QT = QTc * sqrt(RR)
        qt = qtc * np.sqrt(rr)
        
        # --- P, Q, R, S Waves ---
        p_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.16, -0.12)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)
        
        q_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.020, -0.015)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.030)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start
            
            sigma_t = t_duration / 5.0
            dt_t = st_start + 2.5 * sigma_t
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.7) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.035)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.08, 0.12)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.035)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.20, 0.35) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.25) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            amp2_I = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)
            
        else:
            # LQT3: Late-onset T wave (long isoelectric ST segment)
            sigma_t = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.040)
            dt_t = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.35, 0.60) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander (reduced amplitude for cleaner baseline)
    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.05) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.05) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))
    
    # Brown noise for realistic smooth low-frequency drift
    brown_I = generate_brown_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.03)
    brown_II = generate_brown_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.03)
    
    # Powerline interference
    pl_freq = np.random.choice([50.0, 60.0])
    pl_amp = np.random.uniform(0.002, 0.005)
    pl_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    powerline_I = pl_amp * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    powerline_II = pl_amp * 1.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    
    # High-frequency muscle (EMG) noise - kept minimal for clean baseline
    noise_level = np.random.uniform(0.002, 0.005)
    hf_noise_I = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    hf_noise_II = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    
    lead_I += resp_wander_I + brown_I + powerline_I + hf_noise_I
    lead_II += resp_wander_II + brown_II + powerline_II + hf_noise_II

    ecg_signal = np.stack([lead_I, lead_II], axis=1)
    
    return ecg_signal

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
    
    for i in range(N_SAMPLES):
        sample_seed = RANDOM_SEED + i
        ecg_sample = generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx=i, seed=sample_seed)
        
        filename = f"lngqt_sample_{i:03d}.npy"
        filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)
        np.save(filepath, ecg_sample)
        
    print(f"Successfully generated {N_SAMPLES} LQTS ECG samples in '{OUTPUT_DIR}'.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#

# two peaks of the notched T-wave were erroneously split between Lead I and Lead II. 
# Both peaks are now correctly projected onto both leads. Additionally, updated 
# the LQT1 T-wave morphology to be broad and symmetrical, aligning with the 
# clinical blueprint specifications. Adjusted T-wave amplitudes across all subtypes 
# to better match physiological ranges.
# =============================================================================

DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0

    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)

            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_II)

    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: 
# 1. Improved LQT2 morphology by optimizing the distance between the two 
#    T-wave peaks (notch_dist) relative to their widths, ensuring they fuse 
#    into a true bifid T-wave rather than appearing as two disconnected waves.
# 2. Updated LQT1 to use an asymmetric Gaussian, providing a more physiological 
#    repolarization shape while maintaining its characteristic broad base.
# 3. Tightened QRS complex widths and offsets to strictly enforce a normal 
#    QRS duration (80-100 ms), as LQTS typically presents with a narrow QRS.
# 4. Constrained electrical axes to ensure concordant, positive T-waves in 
#    Leads I and II, and reduced high-frequency noise for a cleaner baseline.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(45.0, 90.0)  # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Constrained to physiological ranges to ensure proper projections
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 30) * np.pi / 180.0 # Concordant T-wave
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.22)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.25)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)

        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)

        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, slightly asymmetric T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start
            
            # Asymmetric shaping for a more physiological look while remaining broad
            sigma_t_up = (t_duration / 5.0) * 1.1
            sigma_t_down = (t_duration / 5.0) * 0.9

            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.018, 0.025)

            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)

    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.08) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: Constrained the electrical axes of the cardiac vectors (P, QRS, T) 
# to physiological norms (~40-50 degrees). This ensures that the T-waves project 
# with the correct positive polarities and amplitude ratios across Leads I and II 
# (Lead I being 20-30% lower than Lead II), preventing inverted or vanishing T-waves. 
# Additionally, reduced excessive wide-band baseline noise and adjusted LQT2 notch 
# spacing to reveal the subtle, subtype-specific repolarization abnormalities.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Subject-Specific Physiological Parameters
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(40.0, 100.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Constrain axes to ~40-50 degrees to ensure Lead II > Lead I and both are positive,
    # matching the blueprint's amplitude ratios (Lead I is 20-30% lower than Lead II).
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(40, 50) * np.pi / 180.0
    t_axis = np.random.uniform(40, 50) * np.pi / 180.0
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(40, 50) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Q and S axes are roughly opposite to the main R axis
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(160, 200) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(160, 200) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.25)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.25)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.40)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)

    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.012, 0.020)

    rr_intervals = rr_mean + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * np.arange(num_beats)) 
    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)
    beat_times -= (beat_times[0] - np.random.uniform(0.1, rr_mean))

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)
        
        q_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.030, -0.015)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.040)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start
            
            # Symmetrical shaping spanning exactly from S-end to QT-end
            sigma_t = t_duration / 5.0
            dt_t = st_start + 2.5 * sigma_t
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.7) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            # Adjusted sigmas and notch distance to create a blended bifid shape
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.035)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.035, 0.060)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.035)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.25) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.25) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            amp2_I = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_II)

            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_II)
            
        else:

            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.30, 0.50) + current_twa

            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)

# of wave amplitudes onto Leads I and II. Previously, uncoupled and overly broad 
# axis distributions caused T and P waves to frequently project near-zero amplitudes,

OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"

    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)

    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves

    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)

import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: Constrained the electrical axes (especially the T-wave axis) to 
# physiological norms (concordant with the R-wave axis) to prevent unrealistic 
# T-wave absences or inversions caused by orthogonal projections. Reduced the 
# amplitude of baseline wander (respiratory and brown noise) to better match 
# the signal-to-noise ratio of the empirical reference set, ensuring the 
# critical ST-T wave morphology remains clearly visible. Slightly widened LQT2 
# and LQT3 T-wave components for a more natural physiological appearance.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

def generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx, seed):
    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Subject-Specific Physiological Parameters
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(40.0, 100.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Constrained to physiological norms to ensure positive projections in I and II
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    # T-axis is typically concordant with R-axis
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 15) * np.pi / 180.0 
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 70) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.25)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(0.8, 1.5)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    # Wave widths (adjusted for physiological diversity)
    p_width = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
    q_width = np.random.uniform(0.008, 0.015)
    r_width = np.random.uniform(0.010, 0.018)
    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.012, 0.020)
    
    # T-wave Alternans (TWA) for severe cases
    has_twa = (qtc > 0.52) and (np.random.rand() > 0.5)
    twa_delta = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) if has_twa else 0.0
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Beat Generation (with Heart Rate Variability)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    num_beats = int(DURATION / (rr_mean * 0.7)) + 5
    
    resp_rate = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.35) # Hz
    rr_intervals = rr_mean + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * np.arange(num_beats)) 
    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)
    beat_times -= (beat_times[0] - np.random.uniform(0.1, rr_mean))
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. ECG Waveform Synthesis
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i, beat_t in enumerate(beat_times):
        if beat_t > DURATION + 1.0:
            break
        if beat_t < -1.0:
            continue
            
        rr = rr_intervals[i]
        # Bazett's formula: QT = QTc * sqrt(RR)
        qt = qtc * np.sqrt(rr)
        
        # --- P, Q, R, S Waves ---
        p_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.20, -0.12)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)
        
        q_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.030, -0.015)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.040)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:
            # LQT1: Broad-based, symmetrical T wave occupying the entire ST segment
            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start
            
            # Symmetrical shaping spanning exactly from S-end to QT-end
            sigma_t = t_duration / 5.0
            dt_t = st_start + 2.5 * sigma_t
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.7) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.040)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.06, 0.10)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.025, 0.040)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.25) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.25) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            amp2_I = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_II)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_II)
            
        else:
            # LQT3: Late-onset T wave (long isoelectric ST segment)
            sigma_up = np.random.uniform(0.03, 0.05)
            sigma_down = np.random.uniform(0.02, 0.04)
            dt_t = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_down
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.30, 0.50) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander (reduced amplitude for cleaner baseline)
    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.04) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.04) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

    brown_I = generate_brown_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.04)
    brown_II = generate_brown_noise(len(t), FS) * np.random.uniform(0.01, 0.04)

    pl_amp = np.random.uniform(0.005, 0.015)
    pl_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    powerline_I = pl_amp * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    powerline_II = pl_amp * 1.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * pl_freq * t + pl_phase)
    
    # High-frequency muscle (EMG) noise
    noise_level = np.random.uniform(0.005, 0.015)
    hf_noise_I = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    hf_noise_II = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    
    lead_I += resp_wander_I + brown_I + powerline_I + hf_noise_I
    lead_II += resp_wander_II + brown_II + powerline_II + hf_noise_II

    ecg_signal = np.stack([lead_I, lead_II], axis=1)
    
    return ecg_signal

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
    
    for i in range(N_SAMPLES):
        sample_seed = RANDOM_SEED + i
        ecg_sample = generate_lqts_ecg(sample_idx=i, seed=sample_seed)
        
        filename = f"lngqt_sample_{i:03d}.npy"
        filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)
        np.save(filepath, ecg_sample)
        
    print(f"Successfully generated {N_SAMPLES} LQTS ECG samples in '{OUTPUT_DIR}'.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: 
# 1. Baseline Wander Realism: Modified the brown noise generator to include a 
#    strict low-pass filter (cutoff at 0.5 Hz). This eliminates unrealistic 
#    mid-frequency "wobble" and ensures the baseline drift accurately mimics 
#    slow physiological respiration and movement artifacts.
# 2. Cardiac Axis Correction: Constrained the R-wave axis to [45, 75] degrees 
#    and the T-wave axis to be concordant. This ensures Lead II consistently 
#    exhibits larger amplitudes than Lead I, and T-waves remain positive, 
#    aligning with the clinical blueprint and real visual evidence.
# 3. QRS Sharpening: Slightly reduced the widths and offsets of the Q, R, and S 
#    waves to ensure the QRS duration remains strictly within the normal 
#    80-100 ms range, producing sharper complexes.
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs, cutoff_hz=0.5):
    """Generates strictly low-frequency brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component
    X[f > cutoff_hz] = 0.0 # Strict low-pass filter to prevent mid-frequency wobble
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / (np.std(brown) + 1e-8)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(40.0, 100.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Typical cardiac axis is around +60 degrees. Constrain to [45, 75] for realism
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(45, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(130, 170) * np.pi / 180.0
    # T-wave axis is usually concordant with QRS axis in normal/LQTS
    t_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(-15, 15) * np.pi / 180.0 
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 60) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.25)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.0, 1.8)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.3)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    s_amp_I = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_I_angle)
    s_amp_II = s_mag * np.cos(s_axis - lead_II_angle)

    s_width = np.random.uniform(0.008, 0.014)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    num_beats = int(DURATION / (rr_mean * 0.7)) + 5
    
    resp_rate = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.35) # Hz
    rr_intervals = rr_mean + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * np.arange(num_beats)) 
    rr_intervals += np.random.normal(0, 0.015, num_beats)
    
    beat_times = np.cumsum(rr_intervals)
    beat_times -= (beat_times[0] - np.random.uniform(0.1, rr_mean))

            continue
            
        rr = rr_intervals[i]

        p_offset = np.random.uniform(-0.20, -0.12)

        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)

        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.030)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
        
        # --- T Wave (Exact Physiological QT Mapping) ---
        q_onset = q_offset - 2.5 * q_width
        t_end = q_onset + qt
        current_twa = twa_delta * (1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1)
        
        if lqt_type == 1:

            st_start = s_offset + 2.5 * s_width
            t_duration = t_end - st_start

            sigma_t = t_duration / 5.0

            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_t, amp_II)
            
        elif lqt_type == 2:
            # LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave
            sigma_t2 = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.030)
            dt_t2 = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_t2
            
            notch_dist = np.random.uniform(0.06, 0.10)
            dt_t1 = dt_t2 - notch_dist
            sigma_t1 = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.030)
            
            t_mag1 = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.25) + current_twa
            t_mag2 = np.random.uniform(0.10, 0.20) + current_twa
            
            amp1_I = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp1_II = t_mag1 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            amp2_I = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp2_II = t_mag2 * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t1, sigma_t1, amp1_II)
            
            lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_I)
            lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t2, sigma_t2, amp2_II)
            
        else:
            # LQT3: Late-onset T wave (long isoelectric ST segment, narrow peak)
            sigma_up = np.random.uniform(0.015, 0.025)
            sigma_down = np.random.uniform(0.010, 0.020)
            dt_t = t_end - 2.5 * sigma_down
            
            t_mag = np.random.uniform(0.30, 0.50) + current_twa
            amp_I = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_I_angle)
            amp_II = t_mag * np.cos(t_axis - lead_II_angle)
            
            lead_I += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_I)
            lead_II += asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + dt_t, sigma_up, sigma_down, amp_II)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Noise and Artifacts (Physiological Baseline Wander)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Respiratory baseline wander
    resp_phase = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
    resp_wander_I = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase)
    resp_wander_II = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * t + resp_phase + np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2))

    brown_II = generate_brown_noise(len(t), FS, cutoff_hz=0.5) * np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.15)

    hf_noise_I = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    hf_noise_II = np.random.normal(0, noise_level, len(t))
    
    lead_I += resp_wander_I + brown_I + powerline_I + hf_noise_I
    lead_II += resp_wander_II + brown_II + powerline_II + hf_noise_II

    ecg_signal = np.stack([lead_I, lead_II], axis=1)
    
    return ecg_signal

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
    
    for i in range(N_SAMPLES):
        sample_seed = RANDOM_SEED + i

        filename = f"lngqt_sample_{i:03d}.npy"
        filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)
        np.save(filepath, ecg_sample)

import os
import numpy as np

# =============================================================================
# Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) ECG Simulator
# =============================================================================
# This simulator generates synthetic 2-lead ECG signals (Lead I, Lead II) 
# demonstrating Long QT Syndrome. It models three primary physiological 
# variants of LQTS:
#   - LQT1: Broad-based, prolonged T wave.
#   - LQT2: Low amplitude, notched (bifid) T wave.
#   - LQT3: Late-onset T wave with a long isoelectric ST segment.
#
# REFINEMENT: Constrained the electrical axes (specifically the T-wave axis) to 
# physiological ranges (35-50 degrees) to ensure accurate projection ratios 
# between Lead I and Lead II, preventing T-waves from disappearing due to 
# orthogonal projection. Adjusted base T-wave magnitudes so that the projected 
# Lead II amplitudes strictly match the clinical blueprint specifications. 
# Significantly reduced the amplitude of brown noise and respiratory wander to 
# prevent baseline artifacts from obscuring the low-amplitude repolarization 
# features (especially the LQT2 notches).
# =============================================================================

# Simulation Parameters
FS = 500                        # Sampling rate in Hz
DURATION = 10.0                 # Duration in seconds
N_SAMPLES = 100                 # Number of samples to generate
OUTPUT_DIR = "generated/"
RANDOM_SEED = 42

def gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma, amplitude):
    """Generates a standard symmetric Gaussian-shaped wave."""
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def asymmetric_gaussian_wave(t, center, sigma_up, sigma_down, amplitude):
    """
    Generates an asymmetric Gaussian-shaped wave, typical for physiological T-waves
    which have a slower upstroke and a faster downstroke.
    """
    sigma = np.where(t <= center, sigma_up, sigma_down)
    return amplitude * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - center) / sigma)**2)

def generate_brown_noise(N, fs):
    """Generates 1/f^2 brown noise for realistic smooth baseline wander."""
    white = np.random.randn(N)
    X = np.fft.rfft(white)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1/fs)
    f[0] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
    X = X / f   # 1/f amplitude spectrum -> 1/f^2 power spectrum
    X[0] = 0.0  # Explicitly remove DC component to prevent massive offsets
    brown = np.fft.irfft(X, n=N)
    return brown / np.std(brown)

    """
    Generates a single 10-second ECG segment with Long QT Syndrome.
    """
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Time vector
    t = np.arange(0, DURATION, 1.0 / FS)
    lead_I = np.zeros_like(t)
    lead_II = np.zeros_like(t)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Heart rate and rhythm
    hr_mean = np.random.uniform(40.0, 100.0) # bpm
    rr_mean = 60.0 / hr_mean                 # seconds
    
    # LQTS Severity (QTc > 460 ms is typically prolonged)
    qtc = np.random.uniform(0.46, 0.60)
    
    # LQTS Genotype/Morphology (1=LQT1, 2=LQT2, 3=LQT3)
    lqt_type = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3])
    
    # --- Electrical Axis and Vector Magnitudes ---
    # Constrain axes to typical physiological ranges to ensure correct Lead I/II projections.
    # Normal cardiac axis is around +60 degrees.
    r_axis = np.random.uniform(45, 75) * np.pi / 180.0
    q_axis = r_axis + np.random.uniform(150, 180) * np.pi / 180.0
    s_axis = r_axis - np.random.uniform(150, 180) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # T-wave axis is typically concordant with R-wave. 
    # Setting around 35-50 degrees ensures Lead I is ~20-30% smaller than Lead II (Blueprint spec)
    t_axis = np.random.uniform(35, 50) * np.pi / 180.0 
    p_axis = np.random.uniform(30, 60) * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Vector magnitudes (mV)
    p_mag = np.random.uniform(0.12, 0.25)
    q_mag = np.random.uniform(0.05, 0.20)
    r_mag = np.random.uniform(1.2, 2.2)
    s_mag = np.random.uniform(0.15, 0.40)
    
    # Lead angles in radians
    lead_I_angle = 0.0
    lead_II_angle = 60.0 * np.pi / 180.0
    
    # Projections onto Lead I and Lead II
    p_amp_I = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_I_angle)
    p_amp_II = p_mag * np.cos(p_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    q_amp_I = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_I_angle)
    q_amp_II = q_mag * np.cos(q_axis - lead_II_angle)
    
    r_amp_I = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_I_angle)
    r_amp_II = r_mag * np.cos(r_axis - lead_II_angle)

        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + p_offset, p_width, p_amp_II)

        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + q_offset, q_width, q_amp_II)
        
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t, r_width, r_amp_II)
        
        s_offset = np.random.uniform(0.020, 0.040)
        lead_I += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_I)
        lead_II += gaussian_wave(t, beat_t + s_offset, s_width, s_amp_II)
